Explanation: Reads a whole text file, such as a .gltf model file, into a text value.
Returns a copy of a text value with every match of the first text changed to the second.
Writes a text value to a file, replacing anything already in it.
Loads a 3D model from a file in the project.
Gives an item a collision shape for physics. A Box is set with its width, height and depth.
Sets how heavy an item is, in kilograms.
Joins a chassis to its wheels and drives them, once every physics step.
Says which item is the vehicle's body.
One wheel: a raycast with a spring, set relative to the chassis.
Where the wheel's spring is attached to the body, measured from the body's center.
How long the spring is when nothing presses on it, and how big the wheel is, in meters.
How stiff the spring is. Stiffer springs let the body move less.
How strongly the shock absorber slows the spring as it squeezes and as it stretches back.
How much grip the tire has before it slides.
Whether the wheel turns when the vehicle steers. Usually only the front wheels do.
Adds a wheel to the vehicle.
A ready-made controller that drives a vehicle with the keyboard.
How hard the engine pushes forward, in newtons.
Makes the camera chase the car, 12 meters behind and 5 above.
